    Gallery Trail

    • Three different prints
    1→2→3
    1. Each player solves the same sequence of three different prints.
    2. Match each print's last note to the next print's opening note.
    3. Keep chaining until all three prints are linked.

    Encore Duet

    • Plain sticks
    1. Both players use plain sticks on the last frame to start the duet.
    2. Then take turns tapping the marked frames.

    Coda Postcards

    • Plain glow ink
    • Plain paper
    1. After completing the duet, each player taps a score with plain glow ink.
    2. Tap normally to pick its closing note, or Sneak and tap to pick its opening note.
    3. After both players have picked, either one can stamp plain paper on the last frame.

    Note blocks and chimes are covered in the full exploration guide on the hub.

    Development preview

    Postcard Pairs

    1. Hold a plain echo shard and tap framed signed postcards within 12 blocks.
    2. Your first tap anchors that postcard's chime and bell.
    3. Sneak while tapping to swap the chime and bell for that tap.
    4. Tap a second postcard whose opening chime matches the anchor's ending bell to link the pair.

    Postcard Circuit optional

    1. After an echo-shard pair links, tap the third signed frame with plain prismarine crystals.
    2. All three frames must be within 12 blocks of each other.
    3. Sneak while tapping to swap that frame's chime and bell.
    4. The third frame's chime must match the second frame's bell, and its bell must match the first frame's chime.

    Example: card 1, Sneak-tap card 2, then prismarine crystals on card 3 normally. The circuit closes and sounds Kite chime, Half Moon harp and Ember Peaks bell together.

    Local development preview

    Circuit Conductor optional

    1. After closing a circuit, tap any of its frames with a plain blaze rod. That frame is your starting corner.
    2. Keep tapping the frames in circuit order, then finish back on the starting frame: four taps in all.
    3. Sneak on the first tap to go backward around the circuit.

    No timer, no bystander and no inventory cost. Example on the circuit above: Sneak-tap corner 2 first, then tap 2, 1, 3, 2.

      Development preview

      Circuit Counterpoint optional

      1. Finish a Conductor route on the circuit first. That completed route is the lead.
      2. Then tap the circuit's frames with a plain copper ingot to play the answer.
      3. Each answer tap is one corner ahead of the lead, in the same direction the route went: four taps in all.

      Example: the backward lead 2, 1, 3, 2 is answered with 1, 3, 2, 1.

      Development preview

      Infinity Chord Seal optional

      1. Finish Circuit Counterpoint.
      2. Use one plain clay ball on any of the circuit's three signed frames to stamp the seal.
      3. Use the stamped item anywhere to play its next beat, or give it to a friend.
      4. Sneak-use it to play from beat one.

      The seal keeps the three earned pitches with their opening corner and direction, so it plays the same four beats wherever it goes.

      Development preview

      Seal Cipher optional

      1. Hold your stamped seal and use it on a note block to begin.
      2. Listen to the two voices it plays, then choose the missing instrument from the menu.
      3. The note block is not retuned, and the seal isn't changed.

      Three rounds follow the seal's first three beats. On the example seal, round 1 plays Half Moon harp with Kite chime, so the missing instrument is the bell.

      Development preview

      Cipher Refrain and Refrain Cadence optional

      1. Use your stamped seal on a note block and solve the cipher.
      2. Finish a refrain: the three missing instruments, forward or backward.
      3. Then choose your solo knot. The other two instruments answer it together.

      Example: solo on Bell, and the answer is Chime + Harp.

      Development preview

      Cadence Pennant keepsake

      1. After a finished cadence, use Weave pennant.
      2. It takes one plain white banner from your hotbar or main inventory, once per finished cadence, and makes a placeable banner.

      This browser guide keeps the design only, without materials. The solo instrument is the central mark; the two answering instruments are the side stripes.

      Development preview

      Pennant Fanfare optional

      1. Tap a placed white Cadence Pennant with a plain feather to play its call.
      2. Tap the same banner again to play the answer.
      3. Sneak-tap to restart the call.
      4. Tapping a different banner starts that banner's own call.

      Pennant Chorus development preview

      1. After the feather call and answer on a banner, tap the same banner with ordinary paper to collect its solo.
      2. Collect a chime, a harp and a bell solo to hear the three together.
      3. Different players have private scorecards.

      In this guide, Play call and Play answer do the same with your kept pennant: the solo first, then the two stripe instruments together, left and right.

In game you tap with a plain echo shard and Sneak to swap, and close a circuit by tapping the third frame with plain prismarine crystals. Swap reverses one tap.
